memos.headline: Momentum Leaders S05 and S07 Hold Near Highs While S01 and S02 Deteriorate Below Key Averages
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of 12/19. S05 and S07 are the standout momentum names—both up >24% over 12 weeks with massive relative strength vs SPY (+21.5% and +20.8% respectively over 12w)—though their extreme extensions above the 200d mean (S05 +44.8%, S07 +35.2%) and elevated ATRs warrant caution on new entries. S06 is the cleanest chart near its highs with only a -1.0% drawdown, RSI 56, and positive 4w relative strength, though 12w rel strength is slightly negative. On the weak side, S01 is in a clear downtrend: -10.2% over 26w, trading 8% below its 200d mean, -18% from its 52w high, and showing persistent negative relative strength (-8.5% over 12w vs SPY). S02's -45.4% drawdown from its 52w high and position 7.8% below its 200d mean signal structural damage despite a recent 4w bounce; I would need to see it reclaim its 200d mean before reconsidering.

views.note: Dominant 12w relative strength of +21.5% vs SPY and +25% absolute return with RSI only 53—still has room, but I'd tighten stops below the 50d mean (~$288).
Only -1.0% from 52w high with RSI 56 and +6.3% 4w return; cleanest risk/reward setup in the universe, would reassess on a break below the 50d mean (~$308).
Massive 26w momentum (+59%) and strong relative strength, but +35% above 200d mean and 3.25% ATR make this a high-vol ride; a close below ~$560 (50d area) would flip me neutral.
Solid uptrend with +37.9% 26w return, only -4.4% from highs, low ATR of 1.68%, and positive 12w rel strength; would exit below the 50d mean (~$270).
Persistent downtrend: -10.2% over 26w, 8% below 200d mean, -18% drawdown, and worst 4w relative strength in the universe at -6.8%; need a reclaim of the 200d mean to reconsider.
A -45.4% drawdown from 52w high and trading 7.8% below the 200d mean is structural damage; the recent 4w bounce looks like a bear rally until price reclaims the 200d.
Middling: -4.2% over 12w, -7.6% rel strength vs SPY, and 2.9% below 50d mean—no trend to ride in either direction.
Low volatility name near highs (-2.6% drawdown) but negative relative strength over 4w and 12w; no catalyst in the price action to take a directional view.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Superior Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Face Cash-Flow Compression
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable high-margin growers and names where earnings quality is deteriorating. S10 stands out with 56% net margins, +62.5% YoY revenue growth, and minimal debt at $8.47B — this is the strongest fundamental profile in the group by a wide margin. S05 also impresses with 34.2% net margins, +33% YoY net income growth, and a clean balance sheet ($14.79B debt against $102B revenue). On the other end, S02 posted a 61.2% YoY decline in net income to just $2.35B on $113B of revenue (2.1% margin) while carrying $80.14B in debt — that is textbook cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for. S09 is shrinking (-5.2% revenue, -12.3% net income) with an 8.8% margin and $32.82B in debt, which is another name I'd avoid until the trajectory inflects. I would revisit S02 if margins recover above 5% and S09 if revenue growth turns positive.

views.note: 56% net margin, 62.5% revenue growth, and only $8.47B debt make this the highest-quality earnings stream in the universe.
34.2% net margin with +33% YoY net income growth and low leverage ($14.79B debt) signals durable earnings power.
35.7% net margin and +18.4% revenue growth are strong, though +12.5% net income growth lags revenue, suggesting some margin pressure worth monitoring.
$180B revenue with +13.4% growth and +38.2% net income growth are solid, but 11.8% margin and $55.1B debt keep me neutral until I see margin expansion.
Net income surged +86.4% YoY to $27.47B (26.8% margin), but $90.68B in total debt and only +7.9% revenue growth temper my enthusiasm.
31% net margin is attractive but $427.2B in total debt dwarfs the $46.4B revenue base; leverage trajectory is the key variable.
21.2% margin and +20% net income growth are decent, but only +3% revenue growth on a $22.4B base limits upside conviction.
13% margin with -6.7% net income decline and $31.74B debt on $17.6B revenue is mediocre; need to see earnings stabilize.
Revenue declining -5.2% with net income down -12.3% and an 8.8% margin on $32.82B debt signals deteriorating fundamentals.
Net income collapsed -61.2% YoY to $2.35B (2.1% margin) while carrying $80.14B in debt — classic cash-flow compression I will not pay for.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Slowing Labor Market and Sticky CPI Argue for a Cautious Tilt Toward Duration and Defensives
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime: the upper bound is now 3.75%, down 100bp over 12 months and 50bp over the last three months, confirmed by the December 18 observation. However, CPI is running at +2.7% y/y, still above target, which limits the pace of further cuts. The unemployment rate has drifted to 4.50%, up 30bp y/y and 20bp over three months, signaling a softening labor market that supports continued—but measured—easing. The 10y-2y spread has steepened to +0.66pp from near-flat a year ago, which is constructive for banks and suggests the market is pricing a growth slowdown rather than recession. A CPI print re-accelerating above 3% or unemployment jumping above 4.7% would force me to revisit this call; for now I favor duration-sensitive growth and banks over cyclicals and energy.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from the ongoing easing cycle with the fed funds rate down 100bp y/y and 10y yields down 41bp y/y.
Banks benefit from a steepening yield curve (10y-2y spread +51bp y/y to 0.66pp) which supports net interest margins.
Staples offer defensive positioning as unemployment rises to 4.50% and the labor market softens, providing a cushion if the slowdown deepens.
Cyclicals face headwinds from rising unemployment (+20bp in 3m) but benefit from rate cuts; I stay neutral until labor data clarifies direction.
Energy typically underperforms in a growth-slowdown/easing regime and rising unemployment suggests demand headwinds ahead.
Rate-sensitive sectors gain as the easing cycle continues; the 10y yield is down 41bp y/y, supporting valuations for longer-duration equities.

memos.headline: Earnings-Day Price Reactions Highlight S07 and S03 as Positive Sentiment Leaders; S04 and S10 Stand Out Negatively
memos.body: I reviewed the 8-K filing cadence and immediate price reactions across the universe to gauge sentiment direction. S07 (+11.6%) and S03 (+9.6%) posted the strongest positive earnings-day moves in late October, signaling a decisive upward narrative shift that, nearly two months later, may already be priced but still reflects durable positive sentiment. On the negative side, S04 (-2.9%) and S10 (-3.2%) saw meaningful post-earnings declines, and neither has had a subsequent catalyst filing that would suggest a tone reversal—S04's December 8-K was a board/officer change, not a business update. S09 has been notably active with five 8-K filings since October including two officer changes, which I read as elevated organizational noise that warrants caution until a clearer narrative emerges.

views.note: The +11.6% earnings-day reaction was the strongest in the universe and no negative follow-up filings have appeared, though the move is nearly two months old and likely partially priced.
A +9.6% earnings-day pop and a benign follow-up Other Events filing suggest sustained positive sentiment momentum.
The -2.9% earnings reaction was the second-worst in the universe and the December board-change filing offers no positive narrative offset.
A -3.2% post-earnings drop on the most recent results filing (Nov 19) is the freshest negative signal in the universe with no subsequent positive catalyst.
Five filings in seven weeks including two officer departures/appointments create organizational noise; the flat earnings reaction (-0.3%) gives no directional edge.
A modest +2.5% earnings-day gain and a follow-up Other Events filing suggest mildly positive tone, though conviction is limited by the small magnitude.
A near-flat +0.2% earnings reaction and a high volume of routine filings (five since October) suggest no clear sentiment direction.
The +0.5% earnings reaction was essentially flat; subsequent bylaw amendments and officer changes are governance noise with no sentiment signal.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Easing Short-Term but Structurally Elevated; Falling Oil Signals Demand/Geopolitical Repricing
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 350.41 has dropped 43% over the past month but remains 23% above its 3-month-ago level, suggesting a short-term de-escalation from a recent policy shock rather than a return to calm. WTI crude at $56.22/bbl is down 12% over three months, which I read as either weakening global demand expectations or a loosening of supply-side geopolitical risk premia—either way, this is a meaningful headwind for energy-exposed names and a tailwind for energy consumers. HY spreads at 2.95% are tight on a 1-month basis but have widened 24bp over three months, consistent with lingering credit caution beneath the surface calm of a VIX at 16.87. The 8-K filings across the universe are routine Reg FD and Other Events disclosures with no explicit sanctions, export-control, or supply-chain disruption signals, so I have limited company-specific geopolitical conviction. My base case is that the structural policy uncertainty overhang (trade/China policy) persists into Q1 and I would need to see the EPU index sustainably below 250 or a concrete trade deal to upgrade risk appetite.

views.note: No 8-K filings in the evidence window and no direct geopolitical catalyst; staying on the sideline until policy clarity improves.
Three 8-K filings in quick succession suggest active corporate activity, but without detail on content and with elevated 3-month policy uncertainty, I lack conviction to go long.
Three filings in three weeks hint at material developments, but absent explicit geopolitical or supply-chain content, the structurally elevated EPU keeps me neutral.

No company-specific filings in evidence and the combination of still-elevated policy uncertainty (+23% 3m) and widening HY spreads (+24bp 3m) argues for caution on names without clear geopolitical tailwinds.
Single 8.01 filing offers no geopolitical signal; falling oil prices may help if S05 is an energy consumer, but I cannot confirm from available evidence.
One 8.01 filing with no detail; the macro backdrop of easing short-term uncertainty but structurally elevated EPU leaves me without a directional call.
